tool.name: IdentifyFirstBarriers

param.name: river_network
param.dialogReference: The polyline feature class or layer representing the digital river network. Each feature must represent one river reach with a unique identifier. Reach geometry is used to derive network topology (which reach connects to which) unless Topology Source is set to fields.
param.pythonReference: The polyline feature class or layer representing the digital river network.

param.name: reach_id_field
param.dialogReference: The field in the river network feature class that uniquely identifies each reach. Values are treated as strings for matching, so integer and text fields are both supported.

param.name: barriers
param.dialogReference: The point feature class or layer representing barriers (dams, weirs, culverts) on the river network. Each barrier must have a unique identifier field. Barriers are snapped to the nearest river reach vertex within the specified snap distance.
param.pythonReference: The point feature class or layer representing barriers on the river network.

param.name: barrier_id_field
param.dialogReference: The field in the barriers feature class that uniquely identifies each barrier.

param.name: passability_field
param.dialogReference: Optional. A field in the barriers feature class that records whether each barrier is passable. When specified, only barriers where this field equals the Impassable Field Value are included in the analysis. Barriers where the field does not match are treated as passable and ignored. If left empty, all barriers are treated as impassable.
param.pythonReference: Optional field indicating barrier passability. Only barriers matching the impassable value are included.

param.name: impassable_value
param.dialogReference: The value in the Passability Field that marks a barrier as impassable. Values False, 0 and No are treated as boolean False; True, 1 and Yes as boolean True. Any other value is matched as a string or number. Ignored when no Passability Field is set.
param.pythonReference: The value in the passability field that indicates a barrier is impassable.

param.name: snap_distance
param.dialogReference: The maximum distance in map units within which a barrier point is snapped to the nearest river reach vertex. Barriers beyond this distance from any reach are excluded from the analysis. Increase this value if barriers are slightly offset from the network; reduce it to avoid incorrectly assigning barriers to the wrong reach.
param.pythonReference: Maximum distance to snap a barrier to the nearest river reach vertex.

param.name: vertex_density
param.dialogReference: The maximum spacing between densified vertices along each river reach, in map units. Before snapping, reaches are densified so that barrier points can be assigned to a precise position along the line rather than just to the nearest original vertex. Smaller values give more precise snapping but increase processing time.
param.pythonReference: Maximum spacing between densified vertices before snapping barriers.

param.name: topology_source
param.dialogReference:
Specifies how network topology (upstream/downstream connectivity) is derived.

  • geometry — Topology is derived automatically from polyline endpoints. The start point of each reach is matched to the end point of the downstream reach. Recommended for most datasets.
  • fields — Topology is read from an existing attribute field (NEXT) that stores the downstream reach ID. Use this option if the dataset already has a pre-computed topology field.
param.pythonReference: How topology is derived: geometry (from polyline endpoints) or fields (from a NEXT attribute field).

param.name: next_field
param.dialogReference: The field in the river network containing the downstream reach ID for each reach. Only used when Topology Source is set to fields. The field should be empty or null for outlet reaches that have no downstream reach.
param.pythonReference: Field containing the downstream reach ID. Used only when Topology Source is fields.

param.name: river_group_field
param.dialogReference: Optional. A field in the river network that identifies which river group or catchment each reach belongs to. When specified together with River Group ID Value, the analysis is restricted to reaches in that group, greatly reducing processing time for large national datasets.
param.pythonReference: Optional field identifying river group or catchment membership. Used to filter the analysis to a single group.

param.name: river_group_id
param.dialogReference: The value in the River Group / Catchment Field that identifies the group to process. Only reaches where the river group field equals this value are loaded. Leave empty to process all reaches.
param.pythonReference: Value identifying the river group to process. Leave empty to process all reaches.

param.name: topology_tolerance
param.dialogReference: The coordinate tolerance used when matching reach endpoints to build network topology. Two endpoints within this distance are considered connected. Increase this value if gaps between connected reaches prevent topology from being built; keep it small to avoid false connections. Default is 0.001 map units.
param.pythonReference: Coordinate tolerance for matching reach endpoints when building topology. Default: 0.001 map units.

param.name: write_upstream_counts
param.displayname: Write upstream segment count to river network
param.dialogReference: When checked, an additional field tot_up_segments is written to the river network recording the total number of upstream reaches above each reach (including reaches behind barriers). This requires an extra traversal pass and adds time for large datasets. Default is unchecked.
param.pythonReference: When True, writes the upstream reach count to the tot_up_segments field of the river network.

param.name: edit_workspace
param.dialogReference: Optional. Full path to the .sde connection file or file geodatabase (.gdb) to use as the edit session workspace. Use this when the tool cannot automatically determine the correct writable workspace — for example, when a layer is served through an Enterprise connection that redirects reads to a local offline replica. Leave empty to let the tool resolve the workspace automatically from the layer's catalog path.
param.pythonReference: Full path to the .sde connection file or .gdb to use as the edit workspace. Leave empty for automatic resolution.

param.name: debug_sample_n
param.displayname: Debug: limit to first N reaches
param.dialogReference: For testing only. When set to a value greater than zero, only the first N reaches are loaded during the topology build step. This allows fast test runs on a small subset of the data to verify tool configuration before committing to a full-dataset run. Set to 0 (default) to process all reaches.
param.pythonReference: Limit topology to the first N reaches for debugging. Set to 0 to process all reaches (default).

param.name: out_river_network
param.dialogReference:
The river network feature class after the tool writes accessibility results. The following fields are updated:

  • is_accessible — 1 if the reach is accessible from a tidal outlet without crossing a barrier, 0 otherwise.
  • is_first_barrier_reach — 1 if the reach carries the first impassable barrier upstream from the tidal limit, 0 otherwise.
  • is_accessible_update — Records the result of the most recent run (same value as is_accessible).
param.pythonReference: The river network feature class with accessibility and first-barrier-reach flags written to it.

param.name: out_barriers
param.dialogReference:
The barriers feature class after the tool writes first-barrier results. The following fields are updated:

  • is_first_barrier — 1 if the barrier is the first (lowest) impassable barrier on its reach branch, 0 otherwise.
  • snapped_reach_id — The reach ID to which the barrier was snapped; empty if the barrier was not within snap distance of any reach.
param.pythonReference: The barriers feature class with first-barrier flag and snapped reach ID written to it.

tool.summary: Identifies accessible river reaches and the first impassable barrier upstream from each tidal outlet in a digital river network. A breadth-first search (BFS) is performed from each outlet reach upstream until an impassable barrier is encountered. Results are written directly to the geodatabase: accessibility flags on the river network and first-barrier flags on the barriers feature class. No Trace Network or Network Analyst licence is required.
tool.usage: Configure the river network and barriers inputs, then run the tool. Five steps are performed: (1) network topology is built from geometry or attribute fields; (2) barrier points are snapped to the nearest reach vertex; (3) the first (lowest) barrier per reach is selected; (4) a BFS traversal from each tidal outlet upstream identifies accessible reaches and first-barrier reaches; (5) results are written to the geodatabase. For large national datasets, use the River Group Field and River Group ID Value parameters to restrict the analysis to one catchment at a time.

dataIdInfo.idAbs: Identifies accessible river reaches and the first impassable barrier upstream from each tidal outlet in a digital river network. A breadth-first search (BFS) is performed from each outlet reach upstream until an impassable barrier is encountered. Results are written directly to the geodatabase: two fields (is_accessible, is_first_barrier_reach) on the river network and two fields (is_first_barrier, snapped_reach_id) on the barriers feature class. No Trace Network or Network Analyst licence is required.
dataIdInfo.idPurp: Identify river reaches accessible from the sea and the first impassable barrier upstream from each tidal outlet.
